title: Abraham and Lot
summary: Peace sometimes means letting go instead of grabbing first place. Abraham let Lot choose first instead of grabbing the best land. When sharing feels unfair, this story gives kids a picture of peace being more valuable than winning the first pick.

read_it.prompt: Read Genesis 13:1-18. Watch for what the story shows about peace.

tell_it: Abram and Lot had too many animals for one place. Abram let Lot choose first and trusted God with the result. That is why Abraham and Lot is more than a fact to remember; it is a story with a choice to notice.
understand_it: The point is not that Abraham and Lot is impressive by itself. Peace sometimes means letting go instead of grabbing first place. When sharing feels unfair, this story gives kids a picture of peace being more valuable than winning the first pick.
age_5_7_explanation: Abraham let Lot choose first instead of grabbing the best land.
age_8_11_explanation: Peace sometimes means letting go instead of grabbing first place. Ages 8-11 can follow the story by asking what pressure was present and what faithful response looked like.
teen_explanation: Abraham and Lot gives teens more than a simple moral. Peace sometimes means letting go instead of grabbing first place. The passage asks what faithful action looks like when emotions, pressure, or consequences are real.
key_truths: Peace sometimes means letting go instead of grabbing first place.
Abraham and Lot shows peace through a real Bible moment, not a slogan.
When sharing feels unfair, this story gives kids a picture of peace being more valuable than winning the first pick.
life_application: When sharing feels unfair, this story gives kids a picture of peace being more valuable than winning the first pick.

quiz_questions.question: What detail should you remember from Abraham and Lot?
quiz_questions.explanation: The passage points to Lot. Remembering that answer helps the story teach peace with a real Bible detail.

quiz_questions.question: Name the pressure, problem, or need in Abraham and Lot.
quiz_questions.answer: Answers should name the story's real challenge and connect it to God's response.
quiz_questions.explanation: Good retelling notices what was hard before jumping straight to the takeaway.

memory_verse.prompt: Use Genesis 13:9 as the verse anchor for Abraham and Lot.

discussion_questions: Which person in Abraham and Lot had a hard choice to make?
What does Abraham and Lot show about God, people, or faithful living?
What part of Abraham and Lot would be hardest for someone your age?

activity.title: First Pick Practice
activity.instructions: Use two paper fields and practice choosing peace with a partner instead of arguing over the best spot.

prayer_prompt: Lord, thank You for Abraham and Lot. Make peace more than a word I know; help it shape what I do.
